scope: Post-delivery avoidance event -> one optional native warm refresh; no predicted-prefix initialization
guarantees: Publishing occurs only after arm and base publication and every existing delivery gate
Rejected, startup, reference-hold, terminal-alignment and observe-only cycles publish no request
Four explicitly normal delivered navigation cycles reopen an episode; reference replacement alone does not
Receiver only caches; executed request is one native warm attempt with no random retry and dynamic_repair=true
On failure existing production handler restores published trajectory; optional wrapper restores start/local-target metadata and global cursors
Positive existing safety limit survives successful/failed refresh; zero limit and stop/recovery owners block attempts
Optional notification failure cannot reject an already delivered action
No new configuration switch, driver change, search replacement or stop permission
tested: 10 unittest methods: 9 Python delivery/protocol methods and one extracted-production C++ harness executing 7 distinct cases; exit 0
limitations: Events do not carry a fast trajectory prefix or actual MOVEJ joint-time model
One optional warm deformation may fail; existing safety/recovery remains authoritative
Optimizer budget is not a hard bound on all initialization/acceptance time; actual elapsed_ms is logged
